intro: Searching for the best mortgage advisor near you usually means you want someone local who can look at your situation and recommend a mortgage that fits. You might be buying your first home, remortgaging, or trying to understand what you can borrow. We introduce you to a suitable UK mortgage broker who will quote you directly, with fees on application.
need_heading: What people searching for a mortgage advisor nearby usually need
need_lead: Most people want clear, local advice on which mortgage to apply for and how to prepare.
needs: You are buying your first home and want to know how much you could borrow and what deposit you need.
You are remortgaging and want to compare deals before your current rate ends.
You have been turned down by a lender and need help understanding why and what to do next.
You are self-employed or have irregular income and need advice on mortgages that accept your circumstances.
You want to check whether you need protection such as life insurance or income protection alongside your mortgage.
context: There is no single best mortgage advisor for everyone. The right one for you will depend on your situation, the type of mortgage you need, and whether they search the whole market or a limited panel of lenders. Mortgage advice is regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), so you can check that any advisor is authorised on the FCA register.

When you speak to an advisor, ask how they are paid, whether by lender commission, a fee, or both, and whether they charge a fee for their advice. It is also worth asking about protection, as a good advisor will discuss how you would keep up payments if your circumstances changed.
tell_heading: What to tell us when you enquire
tell: Whether you are buying, remortgaging, or reviewing an existing mortgage.
The approximate property value and how much you want to borrow.
Your employment status, for example employed, self-employed, or retired.
Whether you have a deposit and, if so, roughly how much.
Any credit issues or past mortgage difficulties you think are relevant.
Whether you want advice on protection as well as the mortgage itself.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the mortgage advisor
questions: Do you search the whole of the market or a limited panel of lenders?
How are you paid for your advice, and will I pay a fee?
Are you authorised by the FCA, and can you give me your firm's reference number?
What qualification do you hold, such as CeMAP?
Will you also discuss protection products with me?
What happens if I want to complain about your advice?

faqs.q: How do I check if a mortgage advisor is authorised?
faqs.a: You can check on the FCA register to see if the advisor or their firm is authorised or an appointed representative. It is a good idea to do this before you share your financial details.

faqs.q: Will using a mortgage advisor cost me anything?
faqs.a: Advisors must tell you how they are paid, whether by lender commission, a fee, or both. Any fee will be quoted on application, so you know the cost before you proceed.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a mortgage advisor and a mortgage broker?
faqs.a: The terms are often used interchangeably. Both can advise on and arrange mortgages, but some work for a single lender while others search the market on your behalf. Always ask which type you are speaking to.

faqs.q: Can a mortgage advisor help if I have bad credit?
faqs.a: Some advisors specialise in helping people with credit issues, but not all do. It is worth mentioning any credit problems early so they can tell you whether they can help.

extra_heading: What the first appointment with a mortgage advisor is like
extra: When you meet a mortgage advisor near you for the first time, expect a conversation rather than a sales pitch. They will ask about your income, your outgoings, your deposit and what you want the mortgage to do for you, whether that is buying, remortgaging or moving. Much of the first appointment is about gathering the facts they need before they can recommend anything suitable.

You do not need to have every document to hand for that first chat, but it helps to bring proof of income, details of any existing mortgage, and an idea of the property or price range you have in mind. The advisor should explain whether they search the whole of the market or a limited panel of lenders, and how they are paid, before you go any further. If anything about their answers feels unclear, ask again, as you are entitled to understand how the advice works.

After that first meeting, the advisor will usually go away and research mortgages that fit your circumstances, then come back with a recommendation and an explanation of why it suits you. Advice must be suitable for you, so take the time to read what is proposed and ask questions about anything you do not follow. Remember that we at iComply do not give advice ourselves; we simply introduce you to a mortgage broker who quotes you directly.

extra_faqs.q: Should I choose a mortgage advisor who is close to where I live?
extra_faqs.a: Being nearby can make it easier to meet in person, but location is only one factor. What matters more is whether the advisor is authorised by the FCA, searches the market you need, and explains their fees clearly.

extra_faqs.q: Can I speak to more than one mortgage advisor before deciding?
extra_faqs.a: Yes, you are free to speak to more than one advisor and compare how they work. Ask each the same questions about market access, fees and qualifications so you can judge them on the same basis.

extra_faqs.q: What if I am not ready to apply for a mortgage yet?
extra_faqs.a: Many people speak to an advisor well before they apply, to understand what they could borrow and how to prepare. An advisor can explain what lenders typically look for, though the decision always rests with the lender.
